findings.statement: Gross margin rose year over year in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, to 75.0% from 72.4%, which the filing attributes to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra.
findings.rationale: The filing states a year-over-year increase and gives a mix-based cause. The comparison is year over year only, so it does not show a continuing trend by itself.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased to 75.0% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 72.4% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, and 75.0% for the first half of fiscal year 2027 compared to 66.6% for the first half of fiscal year 2026 due to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra.

findings.statement: Gross margin was approximately flat sequentially in the latest quarter, so recent quarters do not show continued expansion.
findings.rationale: Sequential flatness, together with the reported quarterly figures of 74.9% and 75.0%, means the latest quarter-to-quarter change is not an expansion. This weakens a claim that margin is expanding now, as opposed to having recovered from a year ago.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased from a year ago on improved mix from Blackwell Ultra. Gross margin was approximately flat sequentially as our Blackwell architecture remains the vast majority of our revenue.

findings.statement: Gross margin for the full fiscal year 2026 decreased to 71.1% from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025.
findings.rationale: The most recent full fiscal year shows a decline, with the filing citing the product transition and the H20 charge. Expansion over the annual view is therefore not supported.

quotes.text: Gross margins decreased to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions and a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026.

findings.statement: Much of the first-quarter fiscal year 2027 year-over-year increase, from 60.5% to 74.9%, is attributed to the prior year's $4.5 billion H20 charge, which suggests recovery from a depressed base rather than underlying expansion.
findings.rationale: The filing says the increase was primarily due to the prior year's charge. The year-over-year comparison is therefore inflated by a one-off item in the base period.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased to 74.9% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 60.5% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.
